title: A fast after a feast
odia:
ଅଖାଇ କରିଚି ଓଷା
ଡୋଲିକ ଚାଉଳ ଓଳିକେ ଖାଇଲା
ଦାନ୍ତ ଅଛି ଦରଘଷା।
literal_meaning: Akhai is observing a fast: she ate a dol-full of rice in one sitting, yet her teeth are still only half-brushed.
meaning_odia: ପ୍ରକୃତ କାମକୁ ଲୁଚାଇ ଅନ୍ୟମାନଙ୍କ ଆଗରେ ସଂଯମର ଦେଖାଣି କରିବାକୁ ଏହି ଢଗରେ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ କରାଯାଇଛି।
explanation: The comic contradiction is between a claim of fasting and the large meal already eaten. The closing image keeps up the appearance of a morning before food, although the meal has happened. Read this as a criticism of pretence: the declared discipline does not agree with the action. The journal’s gloss supports that general reading; the connection between tooth-cleaning and the pretended sequence of events is an editorial interpretation.
usage_example: Someone announces a day of restraint after quietly taking the largest share. A listener may recall this saying to question the performance of self-denial. This is a newly composed example, not a recorded conversation.
cultural_context: The verse uses food, an observance called ଓଷା, and tooth-cleaning to make its contrast visible. Its female figure is part of this wording, not a claim about women or religious observance generally. ଡୋଲିକ is retained as a traditional quantity expression; no modern weight or volume has been established.

witnesses.locator: Printed p.17 / PDF page2, Odia example2, beginning ଅଖାଇ କରିଛି ଓଷା.
witnesses.note: Published text corroborates the three-line saying and supplies a brief interpretation about concealing one’s actual nature. Uploaded PDF page1, second saying, is the selection witness and supplies displayed କରିଚି; journal has କରିଛି.

origin_note: A version appears in Sagarika Dalai’s March 2019 comparative article. This dates an inspected printed witness only; first authorship, earliest occurrence and geographical distribution remain unknown.

odia_summary: କାମରେ ନଥିବା ସଂଯମକୁ କଥାରେ ଦେଖାଇବାର ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ।
english_summary: A claim of self-denial rings hollow after the indulgence has already happened.
